plain.text: Abraham moved to Gerar. Again he said of his wife Sarah, "She is my sister," and King Abimelech took her. But God came to Abimelech in a dream: "You are as good as dead because of the woman you have taken; she is married." Abimelech had not touched her and said he had acted with a clear conscience. God said, "I know, and I kept you from sinning against me. Now return the man's wife, for he is a prophet, and he will pray for you and you will live." Abimelech confronted Abraham: "What have you done to us?" Abraham said he thought there was no fear of God there, and that Sarah really was his half-sister. Abimelech gave Abraham sheep, cattle and servants, returned Sarah, and offered him land to live on. Abraham prayed to God, and God healed Abimelech's household so they could have children again.

summary.bigIdea: Abraham repeats an old fear-driven lie, yet God protects Sarah and keeps his promise on track.
points: Abraham again calls Sarah his sister out of fear.
God warns King Abimelech in a dream and protects Sarah.
Abraham prays for Abimelech's household and they are healed.
summary.reflection: Abraham repeated the same mistake. Is there a pattern you keep falling into that you could bring to God?
